# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_SPREAD_THRESHOLD_OPTIMIZATION

**Filed:** 2026-07-21  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** parameter change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

The current ribbon spread threshold of 30 cents may be suboptimal for capturing edge during range-chop periods. A dynamic or adjusted threshold based on range-chop conditions could improve edge capture on J's winner days while avoiding losses on loser days by filtering out low-quality setups in choppy markets.

## Mechanism

We will optimize the ribbon spread threshold (currently hardcoded at 30 cents in the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup) using a grid search over range-chop periods. Range-chop periods are defined as times when the ATR (Average True Range) over 20 bars is below a certain threshold (indicating low volatility/chop) and the price is range-bound. We will test thresholds from 10 to 50 cents in 5-cent increments. For each threshold, we will run a Stage-1 backtest over the entire available history (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) and compute the OP-16 edge_capture (sum of engine P&L on J winner days minus sum of max(0, engine loss on J loser days)) and aggregate Sharpe. We will select the threshold that maximizes the final_score (edge_capture * aggregate_sharpe) subject to edge_capture >= 771. The selected threshold will then be validated with walk-forward OOS (requiring Sharpe >= 0.70) and real-fills validation on the top 3 J days (requiring <±20% difference between BS-sim and real OPRA fills).

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+; $1K paper ~= 14% headline  
2. **Sample bias:** Stage-1 backtest will use the full available history (2025-01-02 to 2026-06-18) for optimization, which risks overfit to in-sample period. We will mitigate by using walk-forward OOS validation.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (walk-forward held-out window to be performed after Stage-1 optimization)  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (to be performed on top 3 J days after OOS validation)  
5. **Failure modes:**  
   - Worst day: if the optimized threshold is too restrictive, it may block all trades on J winner days, reducing edge_capture below 771.  
   - Max drawdown: could increase if the threshold allows too many low-quality trades in volatile markets.  
   - Blow-up scenario: if the threshold is set too low during high volatility, it may allow trades in chop that lose money rapidly.  
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (will compute top-5 days % of P&L after optimization)  

## Pre-merge gate

Gym validators: all relevant unit tests must pass (e.g., test_ribbon_spread_threshold_optimization.py)  
Walk-forward OOS: Sharpe >= 0.70 on the held-out window  
Real-fills: <±20% difference on top 3 J days between BS-sim and real OPRA fills  
OP-16 anchor validation: edge_capture >= 771 and no regression on J winner days (i.e., we must not lose any of the three winner trades)  

## Confidence

5 / 10 -- We have a clear hypothesis and mechanism, but the actual impact is unknown until backtest is run. The ribbon spread threshold is a known filter in the BEARISH_REJECTION_RIDE_THE_RIBBON setup, so changes are likely to have an impact, but the direction and magnitude are uncertain without data.
